paragraphs: The M240i has been part of the 2 Series range since 2014, and across its two generations has used two different 3.0-litre straight-six engines. The earlier F22/F23 cars used the N55 from launch until 2016, when BMW switched to the newer B58 for the rest of the F22/F23 run and carried it over into the G42 generation from 2021. Both are well-regarded engines, and the B58 in particular has earned a strong reputation for reliability.
about.boldParagraph: The M240i is no longer in production, but we continue to rebuild and replace engines for every one still on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre straight-six petrol fitted to the M240i from 2014 to 2016. The N55 is generally well-regarded with minimal reported issues. We service it to the same standard as our other M240i rebuilds, replacing timing chain components, bearings, and gaskets as standard.

The current-generation 3.0-litre straight-six petrol, fitted to the M240i from 2016 onwards and carried into the G42 generation. The B58 is also well-regarded and generally reliable. We replace timing chain components, bearings, and gaskets as standard on every rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the M240i spans two distinct engines across its production, fitting the wrong replacement — or assuming an N55 part will work on a B58 car — risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (N55 or B58) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M240i quote — it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
